data_origin: Own controlled inversion-twinning methods study using a benign 2-butanol molecular graph and one generated3D geometry. Coordinate generation seed31 is a reproducibility choice, not a measured crystal structure or conformational population. All scattering factors, calibration bands, scale/background and recorded intensities are constructed model quantities, not physical beamline settings or experimental data.
stereochemistry_scope: Both MOL records preserve all15explicit atoms and are marked3D; untrusted atom chiral tags/wedges were removed before storage. Determine actual tetrahedral CIP labels from the supplied coordinates and molecular connectivity, retaining zero-based atom indices. ModelB is a spatial inversion ofA up to translation in the periodic representation. Identical connectivity or scalar distances alone cannot establish identical absolute configuration. No optical-rotation sign convention or enantiopurity prior is given.

unit_cell_model.modelB_rule: r_B=(-r_A) modulo integer lattice translations, preserving atom identities. Periodic coordinates are related to the MOL geometries by translation and positive isotropic scaling only.

scattering_model.factor_definition: Each factor is[real,imaginary], constant across supplied reflections. These deliberately controlled factors are NOT tabulated anomalous factors for actual2-butanol. F_A(h)=sum_j f_j*exp(2*pi*i*h dot r_j); F_A(-h) uses the SAME complex f_j, not its conjugate. I_A(h)=|F_A(h)|^2. Under inversion I_B(h)=I_A(-h). Do not average Friedel pairs before assessing handedness.

observation_model: Let x be the inversion-domain fraction relative to MODEL A,0<=x<=1. Reflections from the two domains add INCOHERENTLY: J(h,sign)=u*((1-x)*I_A(sign*h)+x*I_A(-sign*h))+b+sign*d. Parameters u,b,d are COMMON to ALL reflections, with1<=u<=3,0<=b<=10,-2<=d<=2. sign is the stored friedel_sign(+1or-1). Every observation lies within its own closed absolute-error band. d is an unknown direction-dependent additive calibration offset: a nonzero Friedel difference alone therefore does not prove x!=0.5. No Gaussian error distribution is assumed. A separate arbitrary scale or offset per reflection is not allowed.
inference_requests: Form a linear design in[u,v,b,d] with v=u*(1-2*x) and retain its full rank. First solve the central observations exactly and report[u,x,b,d]. Then determine the SHARP complete physical interval ofx compatible with all bounded observations and nuisance ranges; certify both endpoint feasibility. A local nonlinear fit, standard error or grid scan alone is not a certificate of this full interval. Inverting which structural model is calledA maps the domain fraction tox_B=1-x; report the interval relative toB as well. Determine whether the MAJORITY-domain molecular CIP configuration is identified by all admissible data. This concerns the modeled crystal domains, not enantiopurity of a bulk batch or a general sign of optical rotation.
information_loss_controls: Analyze TWO distinct controls. (1) Replace every Friedel pair by its arithmetic mean and propagate its bounded-error intervals conservatively; retain the sameu,b constraints. Report the sharp x interval from these merged data. (2) Set all imaginary scattering-factor parts tozero, preserve the same coordinates and nominal[u,x,b,d], and construct a hypothetical noiseless normal-scattering dataset using the stated observation model. Report its[u,v,b,d] design rank and sharp x interval. This second control is a different constructed dataset; do NOT force the original anomalous observations to fit real-only factors. Determine whether either control identifies a majority hand. Exact all-real Friedel symmetry is distinct from a merely small signal.

interpretation_proposals.A: With complex atomic factors the Friedel opposite keeps the same factors; conjugating the whole amplitude is generally a different operation.
interpretation_proposals.B: The sign of a single measured Friedel difference uniquely determines majority hand even with an unknown direction-dependent offset.
interpretation_proposals.C: Averaging Friedel mates can destroy the information about inversion fraction that was present in unmerged data.
interpretation_proposals.D: The inversion fraction is unchanged when the named reference structureA is replaced by its inverseB.
interpretation_proposals.E: A bounded-error compatibility interval is a deterministic identified set, not an automatically calibrated95percent confidence interval.
interpretation_proposals.F: A majority molecular hand in this modeled crystal proves that every crystal and the whole synthesized batch are enantiopure.
interpretation_proposals.G: Incoherent twin-domain intensities should be mixed before fitting, rather than coherently averaging the complex amplitudes.

reporting: Return coordinate_CIP_labels_by_model as objects keyedA,B mapping zero-based atom-index strings to assigned CIP labels; anomalous_linear_design_rank integer; central_u_x_b_d vector; sharp_x_interval_relative_to_A and sharp_x_interval_relative_to_B as ordered endpoint vectors; majority_model_id and majority_CIP_labels; merged_pair_x_interval; real_only_linear_design_rank integer; real_only_x_interval; either_information_loss_control_identifies_majority boolean; valid_interpretation_proposal_ids sorted. Counts, IDs, labels and booleans exact. Central parameters absolute1e-7 plus relative1e-7; interval endpoints absolute2e-6 plus relative1e-6. Use actual complete scientific evidence, not a final-answer dump.

methodological_sources.title: Absolute structure and absolute configuration
methodological_sources.role: Primary crystallographic methods account of inversion-domain intensity mixing, absolute structure and limitations of absolute-configuration inference. No crystallographic data copied.

methodological_sources.title: Flack parameter
methodological_sources.role: Official IUCr definition of inversion-twin fraction relative to a named reference structure.
